findings.reason: the unit the station stores and the done-when asserts must be (project, session), or the drain-settle node is built against the wrong key and its gate passes a pane that never settles on a peer's work.
findings.text: §10 states "The station records each project's has-live-work reading in its station table on every tick, and the subscriber settles on that reading", but the reading it must stand in for is per session, not per project: `_population_has_live_work(project, *, session)` filters pointers by owner (`if session is not None and owner and owner != session: continue`, crew_follow_commands.py:501) and `_check_settle` settles only when every population in `settle_populations = (session, *sorted(observed_sessions - {None}))` is empty (:1505, :1550), while the done-when repeats the wrong granularity ("the station's reading for its project", :310); a node implementing §10 literally stores one boolean per project, so a session's pane either stays open while a peer session in the same project still has a live run, or must re-derive per-session granularity the station was supposed to hold.

findings.reason: without a control for the "not before" half, the node's gate cannot show the drain-settle guard fires, which is exactly the measure the new sentence exists to add.
findings.text: the newly added drain-settle measure "a subscriber settles when the station's reading for its project turns to no live work, and not before" declares no negative control, and the four §10 lists (sweep-count, advice-settle, quiet-run, and the trace positive control at :316-320) falsify the sweep, the review-settle reader, the beat and the reads, but none falsifies the drain-settle itself: a subscriber that settled on the first empty tick regardless of the station reading, or that settled while the reading still said live work, would leave every listed control green.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every symbol §10 cites resolves today: `review_settle_seconds_remaining` (recovery_review_dispatch.py:1258, reading `auto_resume` alone at :1266), `_latest_resume_at` (:206, returning the newer of `auto_resume.at` and `resume_superseded_head.at` at :91-96), `resume_superseded_head` (written as `{"head": head, "at": _utc_now()}` at resumption.py:1302, empty when there is no head at :1300-1301), `FOLLOWER_SETTLE_SAMPLE_SECONDS` (crew_follow_commands.py:312), `_population_has_live_work` (:482) and the in-flight refusal in `dispatch_review_for_run` (:2154).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the newly added drain-settle measure "a subscriber settles when the station's reading for its project turns to no live work, and not before" (§10:310) has no negative control among the four §10 lists, so no mutation shows the "not before" clause can fail.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §10 declares no gate path inside a scratchpad; its measure is a strace run by the dispatched node, whose log lands in the run's own durable directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags reach §10's symbols or the code it names; references such as "old §81" are plan-document prose, not source.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the new mechanism "The station records each project's has-live-work reading ... and the subscriber settles on that reading" (§10:307) records a per-project flag, but the function it cites, `_population_has_live_work`, is keyed on (project, session) and `_check_settle` judges each of `settle_populations = (session, *observed_sessions)` separately, so a per-project reading cannot reproduce the per-session population the pane settles on.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §10 carries one deliverable: run the review reflex and settle detection once, in the station, on the session's behalf.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §10's plan-section-depends-on declares §7 and §8 (plan.html:23), both of which exist and are the upstream it needs: §7 the station that runs the loop, §8 the subscriber whose reads the measure traces.
